newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates fall on liquidity rise hopes.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates fall on liquidity rise hopes.

text.p: Interbank rates fell across the board as fresh liquidity ahead of the weekend and hopes of a further funds inflow this week eased the pressure on the market, dealers said on Monday.
One-week interbank rate fell to 6.90/7.10 percent against 7.8/8.0 on Friday, two-week to 7.00/30 percent against 7.50/70 and three-week to 7.10/25 percent from 7.40/50.
One-month money eased to 7.20/30 percent from 7.40/45, three-month to 7.25/30 percent from 7.40/45 and six-month to 7.30/35 percent from 7.45/50, the dealers said.

They said the overnight interbank rate's fall on Friday to 6.5 percent, from over 8.0 percent previously after the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill, prompted the fall in other interbank rates.
"There is a little confusion why the rates have fallen so much today," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the market has been tight for the last few weeks and the one maturity was unlikely to ease the situation.
Most dealers said the most possible explanation was the market's anticipation of liquidity improving further this week by nearly one billion ringgit.
On Wednesday, 420 million ringgit will mature from a long-term government bond and, on Friday, 500 million ringgit in Bank Negara bills.
"The central bank has no plans to roll over the funds at the moment, which means the market's tightness will ease further," one dealer said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rose across the board, reflecting the fall in spot rates, futures dealers said.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was steady at 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
But, September was up four points at 92.70, or 7.30 percent, and December up four at 92.66, or 7.34 percent.
